To draw the projections of a hexagonal prism (base edge $30\text{ mm}$, axis $70\text{ mm}$) with an edge of its base in the V.P., axis inclined at $30^\circ$ to V.P. and parallel to H.P.:

1. **Initial Position (Axis perpendicular to V.P.):**
   - Since the axis is parallel to H.P. and initially we can assume it perpendicular to V.P. to get the true shape in the front view.
   - Draw a regular hexagon of $30\text{ mm}$ side in the **Front View**, positioned such that one of its base edges touches or is situated in the V.P. (i.e., resting against the $XY$ line).
   - Project all corners downwards to the **Top View** to form rectangles representing the prism's faces, with the length equal to the axis length ($70\text{ mm}$).

2. **Second Position (Axis inclined to V.P.):**
   - In the Top View, rotate the rectangular top view so that the axis makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the $XY$ line (since axis is inclined at $30^\circ$ to V.P.).
   - Project the corners upward from this rotated top view and horizontally from the initial front view to obtain the final Front View.

3. **Visibility and Line Types:**
   - Use continuous thick lines for visible edges, thin lines for projectors/axes, and dashed lines for hidden edges.
proTip: When a solid has an edge of its base in the V.P., start by drawing the true shape view (Front View) directly intersecting or touching the reference line.
